cls: Topical non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (locally acting NSAID)
pharm: Locally acting anti-inflammatory analgesic with membrane-stabilizing and mild local anesthetic properties; not a classical systemic NSAID by COX inhibition.
quick: Oral rinse 0.15%: 15 mL gargle/rinse every 1.5-3 hours; spray 0.15%: several actuations to affected area
Not relevant; use after meals/oral care for sore throat or mouth pain
Limited data; topical/oromucosal use with minimal absorption - use only if needed
Limited data; minimal systemic absorption with local use
No adjustment expected with local use (minimal systemic absorption)
No adjustment expected with local use
Some mouthwash formulations contain alcohol; avoid swallowing
summary: Benzydamine is a topically/locally acting anti-inflammatory analgesic used as an oromucosal rinse or spray (and topically) to relieve pain and inflammation of the mouth and throat - for example painful conditions of the oropharynx, post-tonsillectomy, oral mucositis from radiotherapy/chemotherapy, and minor mouth ulcers. It has local anesthetic-like and anti-inflammatory effects with minimal systemic absorption. It is not approved by the US FDA; it is widely available in the UK, Europe, India and elsewhere (e.g., as Difflam/Tantum Verde), often over the counter.
indications: Relief of pain and inflammation of the mouth and throat (e.g., sore throat, pharyngitis, gingivitis, aphthous ulcers)
Symptomatic relief of oral mucositis associated with radiotherapy or chemotherapy
Post-operative oral/dental and post-tonsillectomy pain and inflammation

dosage.d: 15 mL used as a gargle or rinse every 1.5 to 3 hours as required
dosage.n: Do not usually use longer than 7 days without review; may dilute if stinging

dosage.d: Several sprays (e.g., 4-8 actuations) onto the affected area every 1.5-3 hours
dosage.n: Follow product directions for number of sprays

dosage.d: Weight/age-based number of sprays per product labeling (fewer actuations)
dosage.n: Rinse generally restricted in young children who cannot avoid swallowing

dosage.d: 15 mL rinse every 1.5-3 hours; commonly 4-8 times daily

admin: For the rinse, gargle/swish the measured volume and then spit out; do not swallow
If the undiluted rinse stings, it may be diluted with an equal volume of water
For the spray, direct onto the inflamed area of the mouth or throat
Use for short-term symptom relief; review if symptoms persist beyond about 7 days
moa: Benzydamine is a locally acting anti-inflammatory analgesic. Unlike classical NSAIDs it is a weak inhibitor of prostaglandin synthesis; its effects are attributed to stabilization of cell membranes, inhibition of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF), and local anesthetic and analgesic actions on mucosal tissue. Applied topically it accumulates in inflamed tissue to relieve local pain and inflammation.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to benzydamine or any excipient
relative: Children too young to use a mouthwash safely (risk of swallowing) - use spray or avoid
Patients sensitive to other oral-care excipients (e.g., alcohol, flavorings)
monitor: Local oral mucosal reaction (numbness, stinging, irritation)

preg: There are limited human data; with oromucosal/topical use systemic absorption is minimal. Use during pregnancy only if considered necessary and follow local product guidance.
lact: There are limited data; given the low systemic absorption from local use, benzydamine is generally considered to pose little risk to a breastfed infant when used as directed.
renal: No dosage adjustment is expected because systemic absorption from oromucosal/topical use is minimal.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is expected with local use because systemic exposure is low.

major: No clinically significant major interactions reported with local oromucosal use
moderate: No significant systemic interactions expected at recommended local doses
minor: Other oral-care products applied at the same time may cause transient local irritation
interactions.food: Not relevant; may be used regardless of meals.
interactions.alcohol: Some mouthwash formulations contain alcohol - do not swallow; avoid in patients who must avoid alcohol-containing rinses.
interactions.diagnostics: No known interference with laboratory tests.

common: Numbness or tingling of the mouth
serious: Hypersensitivity reactions including bronchospasm or angioedema (rare)
rare: Oral mucosal irritation with prolonged use

monitoring: Need for medical review if no improvement within about 7 days
counsel: Gargle or rinse and then spit out the mouthwash - do not swallow it
If the rinse stings, dilute it with an equal amount of water
Temporary numbness or tingling of the mouth is expected
Stop and seek advice if you get a rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty
See a doctor if mouth or throat symptoms last more than about a week
pk: Local pain relief within minutes of application
Systemic half-life ~13 hours when absorbed, but systemic exposure from local use is minimal
Symptom relief typically 1.5-3 hours per application
Store below 25-30 C; do not freeze; keep the container tightly closed
pearls: NOTE: Benzydamine is not FDA-approved; this record is sourced from EMA/SmPC and BNF references (marketed as Difflam, Tantum Verde, etc.)
Acts locally with anti-inflammatory and local-anesthetic-like effects and minimal systemic absorption
Useful for radiotherapy/chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis and sore throat - an evidence-supported supportive-care option
Tell patients to spit out the rinse and not swallow; dilute if it stings
Some formulations contain alcohol or aspartame - check for phenylketonuria and alcohol-avoidance
missed: This medicine is used as needed for symptoms rather than on a fixed schedule; simply use the next dose when needed and do not exceed the labeled frequency.
overdose: Systemic overdose is unlikely from oromucosal/topical use. Accidental ingestion of large amounts (mainly in children) may cause agitation, tremor, convulsions, GI upset, sweating, and ataxia. Management is supportive with observation and symptomatic treatment; ensure airway and treat seizures if they occur. There is no specific antidote.
